title: fix(devx): give the upstream port pin a per-file `ref`, retiring the global one
body:
Fixes #8288

The gate's own header describes the pin as carrying the upstream ref **"per ported file"**. The schema carried ONE global `upstream.ref`, and `resync()` set it unconditionally while updating only the re-synced entry's digest. So a re-sync of one file re-labelled the other entries with a ref their digests had never been taken from.

## The contradiction, verified on the tree before anything changed

`#7749` re-synced the hook self-test to objectstack `70e77ec3b` and moved the global ref with it. The other two entries kept digests taken at `bf10debd5`. Both digest pairs the card names are confirmed, by hashing the upstream blobs out of an objectstack checkout at both refs:

| ported file | digest at `bf10debd5` | digest at `70e77ec3b` | pinned |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` | `449a0aec…` | `274bac47…` | `449a0aec…` (so: `bf10debd5`) |
| `scripts/invoked-as.mjs` | `90f72bf4…` | `6d99f65c…` | `90f72bf4…` (so: `bf10debd5`) |
| `.claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout.selftest.sh` | `fb413bdb…` | `1d8d4458…` | `1d8d4458…` (so: `70e77ec3b`) |

Neither digest had moved and neither ported file's bytes had moved, so all three stayed GREEN — the digest is the assertion. Only the provenance line beside two of them was false. The gate printed, for all three:

```
… byte-identical to objectstack-ai/objectstack@70e77ec3b:… modulo N declared divergence(s).
```

The `#7749` diff confirms the mechanism directly: one global ref `bf10debd5` to `70e77ec3b`, and exactly one `upstreamSha256` line changed (`fb413bdb…` to `1d8d4458…`).

## The decision: RETIRE the global ref, do not keep it as a default

`ref` is now a required field on each `files[]` entry; `upstream.ref` is gone, and `validatePin` **refuses** a pin that still carries it rather than quietly ignoring it. Under the four axes:

- **实际业务需求** — Measured, not assumed. `upstream.ref` was written at exactly one site (`pin.upstream.ref = ref`) and read at five, all inside this one script; nothing else in the tree reads it. Against that, per-file refs have two *named, already-filed* consumers that the single global ref actively blocked: `scripts/check-bash32-floor.mjs` carries a section explaining it cannot be registered because "the ref is a SINGLE GLOBAL field … one per pin and not one per file", and objectui#7953 recorded the same blocker from the other direction. So the per-file ref is demanded by existing work, and a default serves a scenario — several files genuinely sharing a ref — that this ledger has not been in since `#7749`.
- **项目长远合理性** — A ref is provenance *for a digest*. Storing it away from the digest it describes is the defect itself. A default would make an entry's real ref `entry.ref ?? pin.upstream.ref`, so an absent `ref` could not be distinguished from one nobody updated — which is precisely how this survived for months. Retirement makes the pin self-describing, with no resolution step.
- **防 AI 写代码犯错** — Decisive here. `entry.ref ?? pin.upstream.ref` is exactly the lenient consumer-side fallback this repo bans (coding standard #0.1): it would silently supply a ref the digest was not taken from — the bug re-spelled as a feature. A required per-file `ref`, with `validatePin` rejecting both the retired global field and an entry that lacks one, means a future `--resync` that forgot to write a ref produces a loud exit 2 rather than a confident false line. 声明即强制.
- **创业阶段不扩散需求** — A default IS a double spelling: two places a ref may live, plus a resolution order. The standing rule is immediate retirement over a staged window, and there is no named external consumer of this schema — it is one repo-internal JSON read by one script. Nothing here warrants a grace period.

**`upstream.repo` deliberately stays global.** The reason is measured, not stylistic: every entry is a port from the same repository, so unlike `ref` it is uniform in fact, and splitting it would add a speculative field with no reader.

## Migration: this corrects a false label, it is NOT a re-sync

The two entries whose digests were taken at `bf10debd5` now carry `bf10debd5` as their ref, instead of the `70e77ec3b` they had been re-labelled with. **A reader must not read that as a silent re-sync.** No digest changed, no divergence changed, and no ported file's bytes changed. Mechanically, the entire diff on the pin is:

```
-    "repo": "objectstack-ai/objectstack",
-    "ref": "70e77ec3b566b92d7c6551637d6bc746fb840bb6"
+    "repo": "objectstack-ai/objectstack"
+      "ref": "bf10debd587f6ba891be9eadc2b76c91e15bd82b",
+      "ref": "bf10debd587f6ba891be9eadc2b76c91e15bd82b",
+      "ref": "70e77ec3b566b92d7c6551637d6bc746fb840bb6",
```

Changed lines mentioning `upstreamSha256`: **0**. Changed lines mentioning a divergence field: **0**. All three ported files are blob-identical to the base commit. The ports themselves are untouched — re-syncing any of them stays a separate card, as the issue and triage require.

## What changed in the gate

- `validatePin` requires a 40-char `files[].ref` and refuses a lingering `upstream.ref`.
- `main()` prints each file at its own ref, and the summary no longer collapses distinct refs into one — it names them (`2 distinct: bf10debd5, 70e77ec3b`).
- `list()` prints the ref beside each entry's digest.
- The drift message names the ref for *that* file, and says other entries are unaffected.
- New pure `resyncedPin()`, the transform `resync()` now applies: the re-synced entry gets the new ref and digest, every other entry is returned untouched.

## Ablation, on the committed tree, trap/restore, mutation proven on disk first

Every leg proved its mutation reached disk (blob hash moved) before any result was read, and every restore is proven by `git checkout HEAD -- path` plus an empty `git diff HEAD`.

1. **Re-sync one entry, the others must not move.** Re-synced `scripts/invoked-as.mjs` to `70e77ec3b`. That entry moved to ref `70e77ec3b` / digest `6d99f65c…` — independently reproducing the digest measured above. `check-half-states.mjs` kept `bf10debd5` / `449a0aec…` and the hook self-test kept its own, **byte-identical**, and the gate then printed each file's true ref. Exit 0.
   **Counterfactual on the pre-change code** (base gate + base pin restored, same operation): `check-half-states.mjs` came out labelled `70e77ec3b` while carrying the `bf10debd5` digest — the card's defect, reproduced, green. This is the leg that shows the change closes it.
2. **Corrupt one entry's digest.** Gate RED, **exit 1**, naming that file *and its own ref* (`bf10debd5…`, not a ledger-wide one).
3. **Point one entry's ref at a tree its digest does not resolve in.** Gate stays **exit 0** and prints that ref. ⚠️ Stated honestly rather than dressed up: this gate deliberately never fetches (a check that reached `api.github.com` would be red on a network hiccup and green on a cached 200), so it cannot know the digest does not resolve there, and it does not claim to — its summary says in words that the digest is verified and the ref beside it is provenance that is NOT fetched. What the change guarantees is about the WRITE path: no tool path can produce a wrong ref any more; only a hand edit can, which is the same class as hand-editing a digest, which the gate already names as forbidden. One real improvement is visible here: because the summary lists distinct refs, the stray ref surfaced as `3 distinct: …` instead of hiding inside a single global value.
4. **Unmodified entries.** GREEN in the same run as leg 2's red — the two untouched files reported ✓ at their own refs.

Two further legs on the schema itself: a pin still carrying `upstream.ref` is refused with **exit 2** naming the retirement, and an entry with no `ref` is refused with **exit 2**.

## Gates (exit codes captured before any pipe)

| gate | exit |
|---|---|
| `node scripts/check-upstream-port-parity.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-upstream-port-parity.mjs --self-test` | 0 (58 cases, up from 49) |
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/` | 0 (120 files, 3577 tests) |
| `pnpm check:entry-guard` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:lint-rule-coverage` | 0 (no #8369 artifact hit) |
| `pnpm check:comment-mask-corpus` | 0 |
| `pnpm type-check:scripts` | 0 |
| `pnpm lint:root` | 0 (full root scan, 0 errors, 32 pre-existing warnings) |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 — no changeset owed (3 files changed, 0 published source) |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on all 3 changed paths | 0 — **NOT GOVERNED**, none matched |

`.claude/hooks/**` does **not** appear in this diff; the surface held.

## Out-of-scope finding filed

objectui#8385 — this change removes the structural blocker that kept `check-bash32-floor.mjs` and objectui#7953's ported hook files out of the ledger, and `check-bash32-floor.mjs` carries a rationale section that will describe a retired field once this lands. Filed with no assignee, `Blocked-by:` this card. Not fixed here: registering a port needs its blob, digest and declared divergences per file, and for the hooks it also crosses governed surface.
